title: RFSO - Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services in Yukon (Up to 5)
description: This requirement is for the Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC). The Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC), Yukon Region is responsible for managing multiple contaminated sites in Yukon, including Type II abandoned mine sites. In order to meet CIRNAC’s project objectives, CIRNAC requires Hydrotechnical and Geotechnical Services to support ongoing care and maintenance, and advance remediation plans at multiple Type II mine sites and other DTA sites in the Yukon region. These sites have a variety of different geotechnical and hydrotechnical challenges associated with them. The specific scopes for supplying services to each site will vary according to each site’s needs. Works for each of these sites will be issued on an as-and-when requested basis, detailed in each call-up. The work under these SOAs is intended to be consistent with CIRNAC’s Contaminated Sites Management Policy whose objectives include: 1) to meet federal and departmental policy requirements and legal obligations regarding the management of contaminated sites; 2) to require that, where a suspected contaminated site has been identified, the site be assessed in a timely, consistent and cost effective manner; 3) to provide a scientifically valid, risk management based framework for setting priorities, planning, implementing and reporting on the management of contaminated sites; 4) to remediate, based on approved resource levels, all National Classification System (NCS) Class 1 contaminated sites in the North, and Class 1 and 2 contaminated sites on reserve, on a priority basis, unless it can be demonstrated that for a specific site an alternative form of management is appropriate; 5) to promote the social and economic benefits that may accrue to First Nations, Inuit and northerners when carrying out activities required by this policy; and 6) to promote the federal "polluter pay" principle. CIRNAC intends to establish Standing Offer Agreements (SOA) for multiple qualified Contractors to supply Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services for several abandoned mine sites throughout Yukon, including the following areas subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs): 1. Carcross/Tagish First Nation Final Agreement 2. Champagne and Aishihik First Nation Final Agreement 3. First Nation of Nacho Nyak Dun Final Agreement 4. Kluane First Nation Final Agreement 5. Kwanlin Dün First Nation Final Agreement 6. Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation Final Agreement 7. Selkirk First Nation Final Agreement 8. Ta'an Kwäch'än Council Final Agreement 9. Teslin Tlingit Council Final Agreement 10. Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in Final Agreement 11. Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation Final Agreement The intent is to award up to five (5) Standing Offer Agreements for a period from Standing Offer Award date to March 31, 2030, with two (2) one (1) year option periods. Level of Security: there are no security requirements applicable to this requirement.

title: English to Inuktitut Translation Services
description: Limited to firms on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). This solicitation of offer is limited to offerors registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Background Pursuant to section 46 of the Nunavut Act, the Auditor General is required to annually audit accounts and financial statements of the Government of Nunavut. As part of this requirement, the Office of the Auditor General of Canada (the OAG) produces a variety of documents, including the annual Nunavut report, that need to be translated from English into Inuktitut, in either the North or South Baffin dialect. Translated documents will also need to be edited and updated. Objective The objective of this procurement process is for the Contractor to provide timely, consistent and reliable English to Inuktitut translation and editing services for Nunavut reports, opening statements and communication products that will be presented by the OAG to the government of Nunavut. The OAG will also require translation or editing of other types of documents varying in length and topic throughout the year, including consolidated financial statements. The Contractor will perform all work from its own facilities. No travel is anticipated for the duration of the resulting contract. In executing the work, Contractor managed devices, tools and IT services will only be used when processing unprotected information. The OAG will provide a laptop computer and access to the OAG network when the work requires access to protected information. Term The period of the Contract is from 1-April-2027 to 31-March-2029 inclusive, with the option to extend the Contract for up to two (2) additional two-year periods.

title: Web-based Platform for Whole Building Life Cycle Analysis (WBLCA) and Embodied Carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction
description: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. This procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. The solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. At a minimum, the platform shall enable: - Intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - Import and export capabilities for compatible whole building Life Cycle Assessment (wbLCA) submission reports and raw data; - Dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - The creation of an anonymized public dataset. The Platform MUST comply with Government of Canada security requirements for Protected A information and meet Canadian-based data residency requirements.

title: Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR)
description: The evolution of markets from physical trading floors to interconnected, electronic venues has introduced new speed, transparency, and efficiency, but has also created new attack surfaces and systemic risks. Modern markets, which host trading for everything from equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources, can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers. The 2010 United States Equity market "flash crash" and the 2000-2001 California energy crisis demonstrated how weaknesses in a market's public interfaces could have dramatic consequences. Similar design issues in today's complex, interacting market systems could be used to cause economic damage, which the IMR program technology seeks to prevent. The IMR program aims to develop repair methods to protect essential economic sectors against devastating attacks that exploit the public interfaces of modern markets. Current legal and regulatory protections focus on deterring profit-seeking manipulation and ensuring compliance, but they do not sufficiently protect markets from adversaries aiming simply to cause disruption. The IMR program seeks to address this gap by developing the tools to automatically model market designs, identify hidden weaknesses, and recommend and analyze repairs on the market models to make markets fundamentally more resilient to attack. IMR aims to combine Large Language Model (LLM)-based automation with rigorous modeling and analysis to identify remediations for market weaknesses. The program will develop formal notations to precisely describe how markets operate and coordinate, creating machine-analyzable models from informal descriptions like regulatory filings and technical specifications. Against these models, IMR will formulate and assess "resilience conjectures� - mathematical statements about desirable market properties, such as the inability for actors to manipulate prices without risking loss. By automatically analyzing these conjectures, the program aims to prove that a market design is resilient in specific ways or, if it is not, to generate a counterexample that illustrates a concrete weakness. These counterexamples will then be used to refine the conjectures and, ultimately, to recommend and confirm specific repairs to the market's design. This approach is intended to provide a capability to protect U.S. markets against adversaries who wish to cause chaos, ensuring the stability of both civilian and military critical resources that rely on modern market mechanisms.

title: Q702--St. Louis JC Bed Tower IOTA IDIQ
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 6, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition and Activation (IOTA) Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal IOTA Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. This requirement supports VA's mission by providing contractor services to help support the activation. The intended contract type is an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with an eight (8) year ordering period. The VA St. Louis Health Care System - John Cochran Division (VA STLHCS-JC), located at 915 North Grand Boulevard, St. Louis, Missouri, is part of a two-division health care system that also includes the Jefferson Barracks VAMC approximately 18 miles south of the John Cochran campus. These facilities serve Veterans in metropolitan St. Louis, Missouri, southwestern Illinois, and the broader Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 15 service area. The John Cochran campus is in a highly constrained urban setting in midtown St. Louis. The existing hospital infrastructure includes Building 1, constructed in 1953, and the Clinical Addition constructed in the mid-1980s. The campus requires modernization to address functional adjacency, physical security/force protection, aging infrastructure, seismic compliance, parking, and clinical capacity concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM), VA St. Louis Health Care System, and the Kansas City District (NWK) U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) are partnering to provide new and replacement facilities for the John Cochran Division. The John Cochran Major Project will relocate inpatient functions to a new seismically compliant Bed Tower, add new functionality, improve departmental adjacencies, replace aging utility infrastructure, and address physical security requirements. The John Cochran Major Project includes campus-wide expansion. Planned new facilities include, but are not limited to, parking garages, a Central Utility Plant, the Bed Tower, an Engineering/Administration building, a motor pool building, and supporting structures. The project includes more than 700,000 net usable square feet of new space. Clinical and administrative services anticipated to be supported include surgery, radiology, pharmacy, surgical services, spinal cord injury inpatient and rehabilitation services, emergency services, engineering, police, nutrition and food services, dialysis, and additional services as refined by the Government-approved program and design documents. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 29 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 7 December 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. The first Task Order (TO#1 Project Management and Pre-Planning Support) will be included as part of the solicitation and awarded concurrently with the IDIQ. Quotes will be required for both the IDIQ and Task Order #1. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for quotes. P.O.C: Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 below for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 above. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period? USACE SPK DBB Construction - Calaveras Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvements - Copperopolis, CA
description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for the solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential requirement for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) construction services to conduct Copper Cove Wastewater Treatment Plant (CCWTP) Improvements in collaboration with the Calaveras County Water District (CCWD) in Calaveras County, California (CA). The project is anticipated to include installation of a new continuous backwash filtration system to replace an existing filter system; electrical improvements to include upgrading the existing PG&E service size to the main switchboard located in the Control Building, installing a new transformer, raceways, metering panel, new Motor Control Center (MCC), and associated wiring and components; interconnection with a pre-existing CCWD-installed suspended air floatation (SAF) filter pretreatment system; installation of a new continuous backwash filter system to include excavation, shoring, and backfill for a partially buried cast-in-place concrete tank with three (3) equipped filter cells (modules), air control panel, grating and handrailing over the filter cells and feed channel; inlet and outlet piping, valves, and connection to existing ultraviolet (UV) inlet piping; and power and control tie-ins. The project is also anticipated to include construction of a new masonry compressor building on a concrete slab foundation, housing a duplex air compressor with space for an additional unit, along with appurtenant equipment on the compressed air piping including a refrigerated air dryer, oil-water separator, and air filter; a new wet well and submersible pump station to include a new buried precast wet well with an adjacent valve vault housing a duplex submersible pump station, valves and appurtenances, piping, and power control conduits constructed adjacent to the new SAF to convey filter backwash waste flow to the SAF. Finally, the project is anticipated to include demolition and disposal of the existing adsorption clarifier and mixed media filter equipment, dewatering of sludge handling facility solids in three (3) containerized, polymer-assisted gravity sludge dewatering systems that will be positioned on a concrete pad with containment walls and drainage systems to capture drained water and return it to Pond 6 through three (3) quick coupler hose connection points (one (1) per bin), and all associated yard pipe modifications to connect the new components to the existing WWTP, generally buried in suitable native or engineered backfill at depths of approximately three (3) to ten (10) feet of cover. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price construction solicitation issued approximately December 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the anticipated requirement can be completed within three-hundred-sixty-five (365) calendar days from Contractor receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Work may also be impacted by bird nesting season, which runs from 1 February through 31 August. If market conditions indicate the estimated period of performance may be unrealistic, Respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the target price range for the anticipated project may be between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code identified for the anticipated requirement is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue. The Product or Service Code (PSC) for the anticipated requirement is Y1PD, Construction of Waste Treatment and Storage Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that two (2) or more responsible small business concerns under the NAICS can provide the anticipated services, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for competition limited to small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (Deviation), requires that construction small business Contractors self-perform at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor may be required to self-perform a percentage of work if required in the solicitation. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identification (UEID) number or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management / organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page quantity above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Costa Laliotitis, at (Constantinos.Laliotitis@usace.army.mil) by 0800 / 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Monday, 7 December 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number W9123827X1CHG in the e-mail subject line.

title: Pre-Clinical Models of Infectious Diseases
description: Pre-solicitation Notice Information Introduction The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) supports research related to the basic understanding of microbiology and immunology leading to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and medical diagnostics for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of infectious and immune-mediated diseases. The NIAID, Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases has a requirement to provide and develop animal models in order to advance our understanding of infectious diseases as well as advance the development of therapeutics and vaccines for infectious diseases. Description The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) supports and facilitates research that focuses on understanding, treating and, ultimately, preventing infectious, immunologic, and allergenic diseases. The NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) supports and facilitates research to understand, control and prevent human disease caused by infectious agents. Basic, applied and translational research to develop and assess therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics is supported through research grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts. In turn, DMID further supports and facilitates research ongoing under these funding mechanisms and through other programs via an array of preclinical and clinical resources and services to support multiples stages of the product development pipeline. These resources and services include genomic and gene sequencing services, provision of high quality biological materials, biocontainment facilities, and pre-clinical and clinical translational research resources (https://www.niaid.nih.gov/research/resources). The current NIAID Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program is one of DMID�s preclinical services resources and supports the development and refinement of animal models and animal replacement models of infectious diseases, models that subsequently are used to evaluate candidate medical countermeasures against these diseases. In addition, these contracts facilitate regulatory submissions, patents, and other intellectual property applications by extramural investigators who request evaluation of their products. This program serves the DMID mission of supporting investigator-initiated research by providing critical data needed to apply for grant or other funding. Finally, these contracts enable product developers and sponsors to make key go/no-go decisions for candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics. In addition to meeting the needs of extramural researchers, this program provides crucial data to our DHHS agency partners. These data will facilitate the advancement of promising candidate medical countermeasures against priority biodefense and emerging infectious agents to approval or licensure, and, in some cases, eventual deposit in the Strategic National Stockpile. As background, in 2024, 40 institutions were awarded base contracts under the Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program. This program was a re-competition of her Animal Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program, and its overarching goal was to provide capability in a broad range of animal and animal replacement models for use in evaluating promising candidate countermeasures (vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics) against the broad range of infectious agents that are in the purview of DMID. The breadth of the existing contractor pool has enabled a rapid and effective response to emerging infectious diseases, such as COVID-19, and emergency preparedness priorities. Awarded contracts were divided into 4 model-specific pools: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents The Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases program will continue to provide the capability and capacity to develop and employ animal and animal replacement models (e.g., organ-on-a-chip technology) of infectious diseases for screening and product evaluation and addresses a critical stage in this pipeline by bridging in vitro testing and eventual clinical evaluation, including as needed, studies conducted under the guidance of 21 CFR 58, �Good Laboratory Practices�. In addition, for candidate products that are unable to be assessed for clinical efficacy in phase II or III trials for ethical or practical reasons, contracts awarded under this solicitation will enable regulatory approval or licensure via the guidance of the FDA�s Animal Efficacy Rule (21 CFR 314.610 and 601.91). This anticipated �ramp-on� solicitation will award multiple IDIQ base contracts to successful offerors that propose a general approach to the requirements, allowing them to join the existing contractor pools. Successful offerors will qualify for the pool and be eligible to compete for future task order awards in the existing model-specific Task Areas: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents Offerors are encouraged to consider submission of proposals to one or more of the above Task Areas (depending upon capabilities). Contract awards are anticipated to the organizations whose proposals offer the best value to the Government. For the purposes of this solicitation, the following definitions apply: Animal replacement tissue technologies derived from human or animal tissue (in particular lung, liver, immune system, brain, skin/soft tissue or gastrointestinal tissues): Organoids Organs on chips Artificial complex cell systems Microphysiological systems Tissue technologies derived from animals, in particular, non-human primates (for the purposes of bridging data from in vivo models with clinical data) Evaluation: encompasses advanced testing after a product has been screened and demonstrated as efficacious in the same or lower animal models; activities include dose refinement, measurement of host response, pharmacokinetics (in infected animals), pharmacodynamics (in infected animals), and therapeutic efficacy or immune protection against challenge. Model development: a novel systematic effort to reproduce a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent in an animal species following challenge with the agent and includes median lethal and/or infectious dose determination, natural history of infection, and serial pathogenesis studies. Model refinement: a systematic effort to improve the performance of an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by one infectious agent to a different, but related, infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model to optimize its ability to support product screening or evaluation following challenge with the infectious agent. Non-human primate models: new and old-world species, including but not limited to Macaca, spp. (cynomolgus, Rhesus, pig-tailed); Chlorocebus, spp. (African green monkeys, vervets); Aotus, spp.; Papio, spp.; Callithrix, spp. (marmosets) Non-traditional animal models including but not limited to: Domestic livestock: horses, cattle, goats, sheep, fowl Wildlife species: marmots, wild rodents, deer, bats Invertebrates: snails, parasitic nematodes, parasitic protozoa, insect vectors of human disease Aquatic: zebrafish HFIM Pathogens: infectious bacteria, viruses, parasites, fungi, toxins, and other agents such as prions that cause clinical syndromes in humans (surrogate human pathog

buyer: Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics FOBL
title: (26007) 810 HydroSys – Development, Maintenance and Support
description:
The Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) operates a nationwide hydrological monitoring network comprising 260 monitoring stations on rivers and lakes. Groundwater levels and spring discharge are measured at a further 70 monitoring sites. Automated, continuous measurement series are generated at these monitoring stations. In addition, water quality is monitored in accordance with defined sampling plans.

Quantitative data are automatically collected at the monitoring stations and fed into WISKI via the data retrieval centre (AZ).


The purpose of this procurement is to evaluate a tenderer capable of newly implementing, configuring and further developing the new HydroSys system – for the collection, validation and storage of Switzerland's hydrological data – in accordance with the technical, organisational and functional requirements, on the basis of standard software, and of ensuring its operation, maintenance and support.

buyer: Verkehr und Infrastruktur (vif), zentras, Betrieb Strassen
title: K 35 Doppleschwand, Spittel bis Dorfende (Ortstafel)
description:
Die Kantonsstrasse K35 ist die Hauptverkehrsstrasse zwischen Wolhusen und Romoos. Der betreffende Strassenabschnitt ist Teil der öffentlichen Busverbindung der PostAuto - Region Zentralschweiz. Im zu bearbeitenden Perimeter befindet sich die Bushaltestelle «Post», welche zur Linie 221 gehört. Diese Linie 221 führt von Wolhusen nach Romoos, bzw. von Romoos nach Wolhusen und wird mit Standardbussen befahren. Die Busse weisen eine Länge von 11.95 m auf. Abgesehen von der Beschilderung verfügen die Bushaltestellen zurzeit über keinerlei baulichen Infrastrukturen. Im Rahmen dieses Projektes sollen die Bushaltestellen entsprechend den Anforderungen des Behindertengleichstellungsgesetzes (BehiG) umgebaut werden.


Die Ein- und Ausfahrten sollen ebenfalls angepasst werden, da diese ungenügenden Sichtverhältnisse aufzeigen und die Ein- und Ausfahrt im Bereich des Parkplatzes beim Gemeindehaus über die gesamte Parkplatzlänge möglich ist.


Die Fussgängerführung soll insbesondere durch die Optimierung der Fussgängerquerungsstellen verbessert werden.


Vor und nachgelagert zum Ausbauprojekt wird eine Belagssanierung durchgeführt. Dabei werden die Binder- und Deckschichten gefräst und neu erstellt. Im ganzen Perimeter werden lokale Sanierungen an den Entwässerungsleitungen durchgeführt, alle Schachtabdeckungen der ES und KS werden neu.

title: Umbau, Sanierung und Erweiterung Grundschule am Harrl - Trockenbauabbruch Phase 4
description: Das Schulgebäude ist ein ca. 1876 erbauter historischer Massivbau, unterkellert und 4- geschossig. Das Schulgebäude ist als Baudenkmal nach § 3 Abs. 2 NDSchG eingestuft. Das Hauptgebäude enthält die Unterrichts-, Gruppen- und Differenzierungsräume, die Verwaltung, Mehrzweckräume sowie Nebenräume. Im UG befindet sich neben Lager- und Technikräumen ein Werkraum sowie eine Lehrküche, diese Nutzungen sollen im Zuge des Umbaus ertüchtigt werden. In der Phase 1 wurde ein drittes Treppenhaus über alle Geschosse und ein Mensaneubau (mit Musikräumen im 2.OG) errichtet. In der Phase 2 wurde das 3.OG (ehemalige Hausmeisterwohnung und der nicht genutzte Dachboden) zu Schulräumen umgenutzt und eine Lüftungsanlage im Dachboden eingebaut. Die Sanierung der Sanitärkerne mit Erstellung von neuen Steigesträngen erfolgte ebenfalls in Phase 2. Die Sanitärkerne und das 2.OG (Phase 3) sind derzeit noch Baustellenbereich. Ursprünglich sollte das Schulgebäude im laufenden Betrieb in den nächsten Jahren abschnittsweise saniert, umgebaut und erweitert werden. Damit die restlichen Geschosse unabhängig vom Schulbetrieb fertiggestellt werden können, wird der komplette Schulbetrieb ausgelagert. Voraussichtlich kann nach den Herbstferien 2026 die restliche Sanierung starten. In diesem Bauabschnitt (Phase 4) soll das 1. OG/ EG und der Rest des Kellergeschosses in einem Zuge saniert werden. Der Fußbodenaufbau im 2.OG ist ebenfalls zu entfernen Hinweis: Bei allen Abbrucharbeiten sind Feuerlöscher in unmittelbarer Nähe bereitzuhalten.

title: Netherlands – Medals – Medailles en decoraties
description: De opdracht betreft het leveren van medailles en decoraties ten behoeve van Koper. Het handhaven of versterken van de internationale rechtsorde, de vrede en veiligheid is iets waar Nederland zich onder meer militair bijzonder voor inspant. Degenen die zich daarvoor inzetten verdienen bijzondere waardering en erkenning, dit kan onder andere middels het toekennen van een onderscheiding. De onderscheidingen vormen bij het ministerie van Defensie de tastbare erkenning en waardering van regeringswege en zijn alleen om die reden alleen al een belangrijk instrument van personeelszorg. Het belang daarvan wordt met het verstrijken van de jaren steeds beter onderkend. We mogen daarbij niet vergeten dat de heden ten dage uitgezonden militairen immers de veteranen van morgen zijn. Onderscheidingen hebben voor de ontvanger bovendien vaak een zeer persoonlijke betekenis: de inzet die wordt gewaardeerd met een onderscheiding en de omstandigheden waaronder dat plaatsvond zijn vaak van dien aard dat er alleen sprake kan zijn van symbolische vorm van erkenning. Een onderscheiding kan dit dan zeer toepasselijk en tastbaar uitdrukken. Vooral bij herdenkingen en reünies spelen onderscheidingen een belangrijke rol omdat veteranen elkaar ook aan de knoopsgatversierselen of draagspelden herkennen. Men ziet zo in het algemeen wie nog meer veteraan is of men herkent aan de kleur van het draaglint of aan een bepaalde speld de makkers die aan dezelfde operaties hebben deelgenomen. Tenslotte gaat er in de militaire samenleving van oudsher een stimulerende werking uit van het zichtbaar dragen van een onderscheiding. Het is een goede militaire traditie om ook te laten zien dat men zich op eervolle wijze voor Vorst en Vaderland (vroeger) of namens de Nederlandse regering voor herstel of bevordering van de internationale rechtsorde (tegenwoordig) heeft ingezet. Men toont als het ware het goede voorbeeld dat navolging verdient. De meeste decoraties zoals insignes, medailles, linten, strikken, miniaturen en andere uitreikversierselen zijn van een bewerkt metaal met of zonder gekleurd lint. Een decoratie kan zowel vast op het kledingstuk bevestigd zijn, als ook afneembaar, bijvoorbeeld door middel van een speldsluiting, schroefstift of pinsluiting. De onderstaande medailles en decoraties en bijbehorende gespen en batons vallen binnen de scope van de aanbesteding (zie bijlage 3 voor de sub PVE’s). SUB-PVE 01 Herinneringsmedaille Internationale Missies SUB-PVE 02 Officierskruis voor eervolle en langdurige dienst SUB-PVE 03 Onderscheidingsteken voor langdurige, eerlijke en trouwe dienst SUB-PVE 04 Herinneringsmedaille humanitaire hulpverlening bij rampen SUB-PVE 05 Ereteken voor verdienste in brons, zilver en goud SUB-PVE 06 Marinemedaille SUB PVE 07 Landmachtmedaille SUB-PVE 08 Marechaussee medaille SUB-PVE 09 Mobilisatie-oorlogskruis SUB PVE 10 Nieuw-Guinea Herinneringskruis SUB PVE 11 Ereteken voor orde en vrede SUB PVE 12 Oorlogsherinneringskruis SUB PVE 13 Kruis voor recht en vrijheid SUB PVE 14 Luchtmachtmedaille SUB PVE 15 Herinneringsmedaille multinationale vredesoperaties SUB PVE 16 Herinneringsmedaille VN-vredesoperaties SUB-PVE 17 Kosovo medaille SUB PVE 18 Afghanistan penning SUB-PVE 19 Militaire Oorlogs- en dienstslachtoffers SUB-PVE 20 Herinneringsmedaille inzet op afstand SUB-PVE 21 NOC*NSF Medaille SUB-PVE 22 Militair vijfkamp kruis Niet alle medailles en decoraties zullen naar verwachting ook daadwerkelijk worden afgenomen, omdat de specifieke gelegenheden voor het verstrekken van de medaille en/of decoratie zich mogelijk gedurende de contracttermijn niet voordoen. Derhalve zijn in de prijslijst uitsluitend de medailles en decoraties opgenomen waarvan, op basis van de huidige kennis, wordt verwacht dat ze zullen worden afgenomen. Mocht de situatie zich wel voordoen, dan zal de Leverancier worden verzocht om, voor die medaille of decoratie waarvoor geen prijs is vastgesteld, een offerte uit te brengen conform de aanbestedingsdocumenten, zie ook de raamvoorwaarden, artikel 3.4. Toevoegen van nieuwe medailles of decoraties buiten de medailles en decoraties zoals deze zijn opgenomen in het PVE (bijlage 3). Voor deze nieuwe medailles en decoraties geldt het volgende: Ze dienen belegd/ besteld te worden door of namens de afdeling decoraties van DOSCO; Ze dienen ingekocht en betaald te worden door het ministerie van Defensie; Ze dienen voor een vergelijkbaar doel gebruikt te worden als de medailles en decoraties zoals deze nu gevoerd worden (paragraaf 1.1.2); Ze dienen van een vergelijkbaar materiaal en middels een vergelijkbaar productieproces gemaakt te worden als de medailles en decoraties zoals deze nu gevoerd worden (zie PVE, bijlage 3); De maximaal totale waarde van de Raamovereenkomst (zie Concept Raamovereenkomst artikel 1.3) mag door het toevoegen van de nieuwe medailles en decoraties niet overschreden worden. Indien de verwachting is dat de maximaal totale waarde van de Raamovereenkomst door het toevoegen van de nieuwe medailles en decoraties overschreden gaat worden, dan heeft Koper het recht om deze nieuwe medailles en decoraties buiten de Raamovereenkomst te plaatsen en hiervoor een nieuw separaat verwervingstraject op te starten. De maximumwaarde van de opdracht is 100% bovenop de zorgvuldig geraamde waarde en bedraagt 3.305.786 euro exclusief btw (exclusief eventuele contractuele indexeringen). Buiten scope: Producten en diensten die onder de overeenkomst Levering Sportprijzen (medailles, bekers en aanverwante artikelen) vallen.

MARINE RESOURCE TECHNICAL SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE NAVAL FACILITIES ENGINEERING SYSTEMS COMMAND (NAVFAC) PACIFIC AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor/Hickam, Hawaii intends to award Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Multiple Award Contract (MAC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity(IDIQ) to provide marine resource technical services throughout the Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC) Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas worldwide as needed. This solicitation will be issued as an unrestricted procurement with a partial small business set-aside that will result in the award of multiple award contracts that are comprised of two major divisions. The resulting multiple award contracts will be comprised of two major divisions: An Unrestricted Division and a partial Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division. The work shall be located primarily in Hawaii, Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). The Government may also require marine resource technical services throughout the NAVFAC Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas in the NAVFAC AOR worldwide as needed. All Marine Resource Technical Services conducted under the resultant contracts shall conform to the statutes, regulations, instructions and guidelines in compliance with the Request for Proposal (RFP). The resulting contract will include requirements that include but are not limited to, the following: (1) Coordination of Monitoring Projects and Subject Matter Experts, (2) Data Management, (3) Analysis and Reporting, (4) Visual Surveys, (5) Diving and Marine Resource Surveys, (6) Marine Species Observers, (7) Passive Acoustic Monitoring, (8) Marine Species Tagging and Tracking, (9) Photo Identification, (10) Behavioral Studies, (11) Habitat Restoration, (12) Coral Translocation, (13) Anomaly Avoidance Surveys, (14) Event Reconstruction and Environmental Data Integration, (15) Ecological Analysis, (16) Outreach, (17) Miscellaneous Marine Biological Resource Services, (18) Biomonitoring, (19) Biosecurity and Aquatic Invasive Species Management, (20) Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMPs), (21) NEPA, Environmental Planning and Supporting Studies, (22) GIS Mapping, (23) Endangered Species Act (ESA) Biological Opinions, (24) Magnuson Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) Assessments, and (25) Marine Mammal Protection Act. Work will be performed in accordance with the requirements of the Performance Work Statement, and may involve regulatory compliance, planning, analyzing, and various related services on any one or a combination of more than one task order. Exact location of each effort will be designated on individual Task Orders. The entire term of the contract is a maximum of $99 million or 90 months (consisting of a 12-month base period, six (6) 12-month option periods and one (1) 6-month extension of services period), whichever occurs first. Task orders will typically range between $3,500 and $10,000,000. Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. The Government makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, during the term of the contract, a minimum of $5,000 is guaranteed for each awardee under the contract. As task orders are awarded that exceed the $5,000, the $5,000 minimum guarantee will be deobligated and the Government�s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Projects competed to the unrestricted division will require a minimum of 18% of the work to be subcontracted to small businesses. Approximately $68.5M will be work performed in the NAVFAC Pacific Area of Responsibility (AOR), $15M in the NAVFAC Hawaii AOR and $15.5M in the NAVFAC Marianas AOR. These amounts may fluctuate with the potential need for the different types of specific services listed above and whether adequate competition exists within the SBSA Division and those contractors are capable of successfully executing those services. If one or no SBSA Division contractors submit a proposal in response to a task order request for proposal (RFP), the Contracting Officer may compete the task order amongst the Unrestricted Division contractors. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services and the corresponding small business size standard is $19.5 million (which will determine eligibility for awards under the Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division). A MAC is a contract awarded from a single solicitation and may result in award to multiple contractors. This procurement consists of one solicitation with the intent to award no more than six (6) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type service contracts to the offerors whose proposals, conforming to the solicitation, represents the most advantageous offers to the Government resulting in the best value, price and non-price factors considered. The Government reserves the right to award more than six (6) contracts if it is determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Successful awardees will compete for future work during the term of the contract. This is a best value, trade off procurement. The Government intends to evaluate proposals without conducting discussions with any Offeror, except for clarifications as described in FAR 15.306(a). However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions with Offerors, if required. The non-price evaluation factors will be 1) Experience; 2) Sample Project; 3) Safety; 4) Small Business Utilization and Participation; and 5) Past Performance. Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are considered of equal importance to each other, and when combined, are equal in importance to the past performance evaluation Factor 5. When the proposal is evaluated as a whole, the technical factors and past performance factor combined are significantly more important than price. The evaluation of the Price Factor will be based on the sample project attached to the solicitation. The sample project is for evaluation purposes only and will not be awarded on the contract. The solicitation will be available on or about 22 October 2026 for viewing and downloading at the Contract Opportunities website at https://sam.gov/. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Requests for additional information may be addressed to the attention of Ms. Rachel Gerakas via e-mail at rachel.m.gerakas.civ@us.navy.mil, Danika Kamikawa via email at danika.m.kamikawa.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Casey Sugihara via e-mail at casey.c.sugihara.civ@us.navy.mil. Amendments will be posted to the website https://sam.gov/. It is the Offeror�s responsibility to periodically check the Contract Opportunities website for any amendments or notices to the solicitation. Offeror(s) must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov/ to participate in this procurement.

description: Anlass dieser Ausschreibung ist die Sanierung eines denkmalgeschützten Gebäudeensembles auf dem BAW-Gelände in Jülich. Das Projekt setzt sich aus zwei Unterprojekten zusammen: Projekt R - Sanierung Setzungsrissen am Gebäude 20.16 Bodensetzungen im Bereich des Gebäudes 20.16 führten zu Beschädigungen und Rissbildungen an der Gebäudekonstruktion und an Oberflächen. description: Der Südwestrundfunk (SWR) beabsichtigt, für seine Liegenschaft am Standort Mainz eine Rahmenvereinbarung über die Durchführung von Wartungs-, Reparatur- und Notdienstleistungen für die haustechnischen Anlagen der Gewerke Heizung, Lüftung, Sanitär und Kälte (HLSK) abzuschließen. Die haustechnischen Anlagen stellen eine wesentliche Voraussetzung für die Aufrechterhaltung des Gebäudebetriebs sowie die Sicherstellung der betrieblichen Abläufe am Standort Mainz dar. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist die dauerhafte Gewährleistung der Funktionsfähigkeit, Betriebssicherheit und Verfügbarkeit der vorhandenen technischen Anlagen. Gegenstand des Vergabeverfahrens ist die Vergabe der nachfolgenden drei Leistungsbereiche: 1. Wartungsleistungen Regelmäßige, planmäßige und fachgerechte Durchführung der im Leistungsverzeichnis beschriebenen Wartungsleistungen an den vorhandenen haustechnischen Anlagen. Hierzu gehören insbesondere die erforderlichen Prüfungen, Funktionskontrollen und Wartungsmaßnahmen einschließlich der Dokumentation der durchgeführten Arbeiten. 2. Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsleistungen Bedarfsabhängige Durchführung von Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsleistungen zur Behebung festgestellter Mängel und Störungen sowie zur Wiederherstellung der ordnungsgemäßen Funktionsfähigkeit der technischen Anlagen. Die Beauftragung erfolgt grundsätzlich nach gesonderter Freigabe durch den Auftraggeber. Die Abrechnung erfolgt auf Grundlage der im Leistungsverzeichnis angebotenen Einheitspreise beziehungsweise Stundenverrechnungssätze. 3. Notdienstbereitschaft und Notdiensteinsätze Vorhaltung und Organisation eines Notdienstes zur Entgegennahme und Bearbeitung dringender technischer Störungen außerhalb der regulären Betriebszeiten. Die Notdienstbereitschaft ist insbesondere werktags von 16:00 Uhr bis 07:00 Uhr, an Wochenenden von Freitag 16:00 Uhr bis Montag 07:00 Uhr sowie an Feiertagen ganztägig sicherzustellen. Bei einem als Notfall eingestuften Ereignis muss qualifiziertes Fachpersonal spätestens innerhalb von 60 Minuten nach Eingang der Störungsmeldung am betroffenen Leistungsort eintreffen. Die Vorhaltung der Notdienstbereitschaft wird über eine gesonderte Bereitschaftspauschale vergütet. Tatsächliche Notdiensteinsätze werden nach den vereinbarten Stundenverrechnungssätzen und Zuschlägen abgerechnet. Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen umfassen darüber hinaus die Abstimmung und Koordination mit dem Auftraggeber, eine transparente Wartungsplanung, die Nachverfolgung von Störungsmeldungen sowie die nachvollziehbare Dokumentation sämtlicher durchgeführter Leistungen. Die Vergabe erfolgt als Gesamtauftrag an einen Auftragnehmer. Es ist vorgesehen, eine Rahmenvereinbarung mit einer Grundlaufzeit von 24 Monaten abzuschließen. Dem Auftraggeber wird das einseitige Recht eingeräumt, die Rahmenvereinbarung einmalig um weitere 24 Monate zu verlängern. Die maximale Vertragslaufzeit beträgt somit 48 Monate. Die konkreten Leistungsanforderungen, Anlagen, Wartungsintervalle, Mengenansätze, Ausführungsbedingungen, Preispositionen und Abrechnungsmodalitäten ergeben sich aus dem Leistungsverzeichnis (Anlage 02) einschließlich der zugehörigen Vorbemerkungen sowie den weiteren Verfahrens- und Vertragsunterlagen. Die im Leistungsverzeichnis angegebenen kalkulatorischen Mengen und Wertungsansätze dienen der einheitlichen Angebotskalkulation und Preiswertung. Sie begründen keinen Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf Abruf bestimmter Mengen, soweit keine verbindlichen Mindestabnahmemengen ausdrücklich vereinbart sind.

title: Evaluierung von Promillegrenzen für Fahrrad- und Pedelec-Fahrende
description: Die sichere Teilnahme am Straßenverkehr setzt eine zuverlässige Gefahrenwahrnehmung sowie angemessene Verhaltensreaktionen voraus. Bereits bei niedrigen Alkoholkonzentrationen werden diese Fähigkeiten beeinträchtigt, wodurch das Unfallrisiko mit zunehmendem Alkoholisierungsgrad exponentiell ansteigt. Während sich die bisherige wissenschaftliche Forschung und die rechtlichen Regelungen überwiegend auf Kraftfahrzeugführende konzentrieren, bestehen für Radfahrende weiterhin rechtliche Besonderheiten: Eine absolute Fahruntüchtigkeit wird erst ab einer Blutalkoholkonzentration von 1,6 ‰ angenommen, zudem existiert kein eigenständiger Bußgeldtatbestand für alkoholisiertes Radfahren. Vor dem Hintergrund der stark gestiegenen Fahrrad- und Pedelec-Nutzung und damit verbundenen höheren Unfallrisikos sowie steigender Nutzungs- und Unfallzahlen gewinnt die Frage nach einer Anpassung der rechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen an Bedeutung. Ziel ist es, einen Beitrag zur Erhöhung der Verkehrssicherheit und zur Umsetzung der Vision Zero zu leisten.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistung Busbahnhof Hamm-Brücher-Platz
description: Die Ausschreibung beinhaltet die Planung zur Neugestaltung des Hamm-Brücher-Platzes am Marburger Südbahnhof, der aktuell und zukünftig als ein zentraler Omnibusbahnhof (ZOB) genutzt wird. Der Hamm-Brücher-Platz hat im Übergang zwischen Schienen- und Busverkehr und als Umsteigehaltestelle eine entscheidende Bedeutung für den Öffentlichen Personennahverkehr in Marburg. Der ZOB soll als ein Mobility Hub mit einer übersichtlichen und nachvollziehbaren Steuerung aller Verkehrsteilnehmenden realisiert werden. Die Umgestaltung der Verkehrsanlagen steht in unmittelbarem Zusammenhang zum geplanten Ersatzneubau des Hamm-Brücher-Stegs, der Südbahnhof und ZOB über die Gleisanlagen der Main-Weser-Bahn und die Bundesstraße 3 mit der Kernstadt sowie Bus-Umsteigehaltestellen untereinander verbindet. Bestandteil der Planung ist die landschaftsarchitektonische Einbindung der Verkehrsanlagen in die Übergangsbereiche zwischen Hamm-Brücher-Steg und Grünraum. Die Stadt Marburg hat im Jahr 2025 eine Machbarkeitsstudie und Planung erstellen lassen, um die Kosten und den Aufwand für den barrierefreien Ersatzneubau des Stegs zu ermitteln und mögliche Fördermöglichkeiten sowie die zukünftige Zusammenarbeit mit der Deutschen Bahn und Hessen Mobil zu eruieren. Im Rahmen dieser Untersuchungen und Planungen wurde der ZOB ebenfalls bearbeitet. Die weiteren Planungen sollen auf diesen Ergebnissen aufbauen. Die Bauausführung des Hamm-Brücher-Plates muss zeitlich und logistisch auch auf den Bau des Hamm-Brücher-Steges abgestimmt werden. Die Bearbeitung hat unmittelbar nach Auftragserteilung zu beginnen. Die Leistung wird in zwei Fachlose (Verkehrsflächen und Freianlagen) aufgeteilt. Eine Bewerbung bzw. Angebotsabgabe ist nur für beide Lose gemeinsam zulässig. Der Zuschlag wird nur an einen Auftragnehmer bzw. eine Bewerber-/Bietergemeinschaft für beide Lose erteilt. Voraussichtliche Laufzeit bis 2031/2032

title: Gebäude 20.16: Sanierung Setzungsschäden Gebäude 20.16 - 20.18: Brandschutzsanierung (Gebäude 20.16 - 20.18: Denkmalgeschützte Unterrichtsgebäude) Objektplanung
description: Anlass dieser Ausschreibung ist die Sanierung eines denkmalgeschützten Gebäudeensembles auf dem BAW-Gelände in Jülich. Mit diesem Dokument werden die Leistungen der Objektplanung für die Leistungsphasen 5 - 8 unter Beachtung des aktuellen Gebäudeenergiegesetzes (GEG) und der zugrundeliegenden Entwurfsplanung angefragt. Das Projekt setzt sich aus zwei Unterprojekten zusammen: Projekt R - Sanierung Setzungsrissen am Gebäude 20.16 Bodensetzungen im Bereich des Gebäudes 20.16 führten zu Beschädigungen und Rissbildungen an der Gebäudekonstruktion und an Oberflächen. Es wurde eine Baugrundverstärkung durchgeführt, die die Setzungsbewegungen zum Stillstand gebracht haben. Inhalt dieser Planungsleistung ist die Sanierung der Folgeschäden: • die Risssanierung an Wänden und Decken, • die Fassadensanierung inkl. Dachüberstand, • die statisch notwendige Ertüchtigung loser Steintreppenelemente, • die Funktionsprüfung bzw. Erneuerung von Fenstern, Türen und Sonnenschutzelementen, • Putz- und Malerarbeiten, • Bodenbelagsarbeiten, • Dachdeckerarbeiten. Projekt B - Brandschutzsanierung Gebäude 20.16 - 20.18 Da die Bauantragsunterlagen aus der Bauzeit und Genehmigungsunterlagen, die im Rahmen der verschiedenen Nutzungsänderungen erstellt wurden, nur in geringem Maße vorliegen, wurde zur Erstellung eines neuen Brandschutzkonzeptes eine Bewertung des Bestandes und des Bestandschutzes für die Gebäude vorgenommen. Das nun vorliegende Brandschutzkonzept stuft die Gebäude 20.16 bis 20.18 gemäß §2 (3) BauO NRW 2018 als Gebäude der Gebäudeklasse 5 sowie als bauliche Anlage besonderer Art oder Nutzung (Sonderbau) ein. Inhalt dieser Planungsleistung sind die aus dem Brandschutzkonzept resultierenden Arbeiten zur: • brandschutztechnischen Ertüchtigung, • Herstellung erforderlicher Rettungswege Schaffung notwendiger Brandabschottungen.

Stručný opis projektu 6.1. SE ako významný výrobca elektrickej energie v Slovenskej republike pripravuje projekt Modernizácia bezpečnostných systémov SORR, SIS a CPL na blokoch EMO12. 6.2. Projekt predstavuje komplexnú modernizáciu vybraných bezpečnostných systémov jadrovej elektrárne, ktorých účelom je zabezpečenie plnenia bezpečnostných funkcií, ochrany reaktora, ochrany technologických zariadení a riadenia bezpečnostne významných funkcií v podmienkach normálnej prevádzky, abnormálnej prevádzky a projektových udalostí. 6.3. Predmetom projektu je najmä návrh, projektovanie, kvalifikácia, dodávka, montáž, skúšky, uvedenie do prevádzky a odovzdanie modernizovaných systémov SORR, SIS a CPL vrátane potrebných úprav súvisiacich zariadení, rozhraní, káblových trás, napájania, dokumentácie, skúšobných postupov, prevádzkových predpisov, výcviku a podpory počas uvádzania do prevádzky. 6.4. Projekt musí byť realizovaný tak, aby boli počas prípravy a realizácie rešpektované najmä tieto základné princípy: 6.4.1. zachovanie jadrovej bezpečnosti počas celého životného cyklu projektu a minimalizácia dopadov na bezpečnú a spoľahlivú prevádzku blokov EMO12; 6.4.2. realizácia prác v súlade s plánovanými odstávkami, prevádzkovými obmedzeniami a požiadavkami elektrárne; 6.4.3. preukázateľná kvalifikácia navrhovaných zariadení, systémov, softvéru, hardvéru a jednoznačná nadväznosť technického riešenia na existujúcu licenčnú, projektovú a prevádzkovú dokumentáciu; 6.4.4. riadenie technických, integračných, licenčných, kvalifikačných, kybernetických, realizačných a harmonogramových rizík a zabezpečenie dlhodobej servisnej podpory a technickej podpory modernizovaných systémov. 6.5. Cieľom projektu je pripraviť a realizovať také technické riešenie, ktoré bude zodpovedať bezpečnostnému významu modernizovaných systémov, bude realizovateľné v podmienkach prevádzkovanej jadrovej elektrárne, bude licenčne obhájiteľné, ekonomicky primerané a bude poskytovať dostatočnú technickú a prevádzkovú stabilitu počas ďalšej plánovanej prevádzky blokov EMO12. 6.6. Projekt si vzhľadom na svoj rozsah, bezpečnostný význam, počet rozhraní, väzbu na odstávky a licenčné požiadavky vyžaduje detailné technické prerokovanie s Uchádzačmi v rámci súťažného dialógu.

title: New Fire Station and Municipal Operations Building, BKP 463 Landscaping Works
description:
The existing fire station, the municipal maintenance depot integrated within it (maintenance and forestry services), as well as the main recycling centre, water utility facilities, and various civil protection installations located elsewhere in Illnau-Effretikon, no longer meet current requirements.

These municipal services and the facilities they require are therefore to be consolidated on a centrally located site within the Eselriet area, on the outskirts of Effretikon. The new Eselriet location provides the opportunity to fully accommodate the needs identified by the Departments of Public Safety and Civil Engineering.

A new fire station and municipal operations building is therefore planned for the site. It will serve the Department of Public Safety (Fire Service, Emergency Services, and Civil Protection) as well as the Department of Civil Engineering (Maintenance Services, Forestry and Nature Conservation, Waste Management, and Water Supply).

The objective is to create a sustainable, future-oriented, and functional facility that generates synergies and brings together the needs of the Fire Service, Civil Protection, Maintenance Services, Forestry Services, the Main Recycling Centre, and the Water Supply Department within a single integrated complex.

buyer: Syndicat intercommunal pour la Step de la Saunerie
title: GC 01B Installation de chantier - Step de la Saunerie - Colombier
description:
Le présent marché porte sur les travaux d’installations de chantier, de génie civil des réseaux et des travaux spéciaux et comprend :

Installations de chantier communes :

  • Fourniture, installation, superposition, entretien et repli des conteneurs dédiés à la base de vie commune ainsi que des aires de stockage.
  • Mise en place de raccordements temporaires en eau, électricité et évacuation des eaux de chantier, pose de clôtures et signalisation et aménagement des pistes d’accès.

Génie civil des réseaux et sous-station :

  • Réalisation des fouilles en tranchées, lits de pose, pose de tubes de protection et remblayage pour les conduites souterraines (eau potable, gaz naturel, électricité).
  • Génie civil Groupe E. Construction sur site des structures en béton de la nouvelle station transformatrice (fosse, radier, chambre de tirage, étanchéité).

Travaux spéciaux et protection d’ouvrages :

  • Forage et bétonnage de profilés métalliques verticaux dans le terrain, suivi du montage, de l’entretien et du démontage d’une paroi de protection métallique le long de la voie ferrée TransN.
  • Exécution de micropieux forés et tubés pour les fondations de la station transformatrice Groupe E.

Gestion environnementale

  • Installation et exploitation de bassins de décantation et d’unités de neutralisation du pH pour le traitement des eaux de chantier avant rejet.
  • Réalisation de sondages, tri sélectif, transport et évacuation en décharge contrôlée des déblais et matériaux excavés, avec traitement spécifique des terres polluées (OLED et PFAS).

Le bâtiment fera l’objet d’une rénovation complète, d’une modernisation technique et sera adapté aux exigences actuelles et futures en matière d’utilisation, de flexibilité, de durabilité, de sécurité et de rentabilité.

Le projet tient compte de l’ouverture progressive du site Rosental, de son intégration urbanistique ainsi que d’un accès et d’un approvisionnement autonomes du bâtiment, indépendants du site.

L’objectif est de créer un bâtiment durable, de haute qualité et rentable, capable de s’adapter aux différents besoins des locataires.

title: 2026-44-BAU-EU-X Rahmenvereinbarung für die Durchführung von Reparatur- und Wartungsleistungen für die Haustechnik (Heizung, Sanitär, Lüftung, Kälte) am SWR-Standort Mainz
description: Der Südwestrundfunk (SWR) beabsichtigt, für seine Liegenschaft am Standort Mainz eine Rahmenvereinbarung über die Durchführung von Wartungs-, Reparatur- und Notdienstleistungen für die haustechnischen Anlagen der Gewerke Heizung, Lüftung, Sanitär und Kälte (HLSK) abzuschließen. Die haustechnischen Anlagen stellen eine wesentliche Voraussetzung für die Aufrechterhaltung des Gebäudebetriebs sowie die Sicherstellung der betrieblichen Abläufe am Standort Mainz dar. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist die dauerhafte Gewährleistung der Funktionsfähigkeit, Betriebssicherheit und Verfügbarkeit der vorhandenen technischen Anlagen. Gegenstand des Vergabeverfahrens ist die Vergabe der nachfolgenden drei Leistungsbereiche: 1. Wartungsleistungen Regelmäßige, planmäßige und fachgerechte Durchführung der im Leistungsverzeichnis beschriebenen Wartungsleistungen an den vorhandenen haustechnischen Anlagen. Hierzu gehören insbesondere die erforderlichen Prüfungen, Funktionskontrollen und Wartungsmaßnahmen einschließlich der Dokumentation der durchgeführten Arbeiten. 2. Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsleistungen Bedarfsabhängige Durchführung von Reparatur- und Instandsetzungsleistungen zur Behebung festgestellter Mängel und Störungen sowie zur Wiederherstellung der ordnungsgemäßen Funktionsfähigkeit der technischen Anlagen. Die Beauftragung erfolgt grundsätzlich nach gesonderter Freigabe durch den Auftraggeber. Die Abrechnung erfolgt auf Grundlage der im Leistungsverzeichnis angebotenen Einheitspreise beziehungsweise Stundenverrechnungssätze. 3. Notdienstbereitschaft und Notdiensteinsätze Vorhaltung und Organisation eines Notdienstes zur Entgegennahme und Bearbeitung dringender technischer Störungen außerhalb der regulären Betriebszeiten. Die Notdienstbereitschaft ist insbesondere werktags von 16:00 Uhr bis 07:00 Uhr, an Wochenenden von Freitag 16:00 Uhr bis Montag 07:00 Uhr sowie an Feiertagen ganztägig sicherzustellen. Bei einem als Notfall eingestuften Ereignis muss qualifiziertes Fachpersonal spätestens innerhalb von 60 Minuten nach Eingang der Störungsmeldung am betroffenen Leistungsort eintreffen. Die Vorhaltung der Notdienstbereitschaft wird über eine gesonderte Bereitschaftspauschale vergütet. Tatsächliche Notdiensteinsätze werden nach den vereinbarten Stundenverrechnungssätzen und Zuschlägen abgerechnet. Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen umfassen darüber hinaus die Abstimmung und Koordination mit dem Auftraggeber, eine transparente Wartungsplanung, die Nachverfolgung von Störungsmeldungen sowie die nachvollziehbare Dokumentation sämtlicher durchgeführter Leistungen. Die Vergabe erfolgt als Gesamtauftrag an einen Auftragnehmer. Es ist vorgesehen, eine Rahmenvereinbarung mit einer Grundlaufzeit von 24 Monaten abzuschließen. Dem Auftraggeber wird das einseitige Recht eingeräumt, die Rahmenvereinbarung einmalig um weitere 24 Monate zu verlängern. Die maximale Vertragslaufzeit beträgt somit 48 Monate. Die konkreten Leistungsanforderungen, Anlagen, Wartungsintervalle, Mengenansätze, Ausführungsbedingungen, Preispositionen und Abrechnungsmodalitäten ergeben sich aus dem Leistungsverzeichnis (Anlage 02) einschließlich der zugehörigen Vorbemerkungen sowie den weiteren Verfahrens- und Vertragsunterlagen. Die im Leistungsverzeichnis angegebenen kalkulatorischen Mengen und Wertungsansätze dienen der einheitlichen Angebotskalkulation und Preiswertung. Sie begründen keinen Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf Abruf bestimmter Mengen, soweit keine verbindlichen Mindestabnahmemengen ausdrücklich vereinbart sind.

title: Mediator Consultant - Saskatchewan for the Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS)
description: The Programs Branch (PB) of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) has requirements on an "as and when requested" basis for professional resources with expertise and skillsets for the delivery of financial counselling and mediation services. This requirement is to establish a Task Authorization Contract with a qualified Contractor's for services in Saskatchewan. It is intended to result in the award of 5 (five) contracts for 5 (five) years. The Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS) offers free financial counselling and mediation services to farmers who are having difficulties meeting their financial obligations. It is a voluntary, private and confidential service that brings farmers and their creditors together with a Mediator in a neutral forum to reach a mutually acceptable solution. The FDMS Administrator will assign a Financial Consultant and a Mediator to work with the farmer through the mediation process. Confidentiality is extremely important to the quality and effectiveness of the service. Information obtained from the farmer and their creditor(s) is used for the sole purpose of mediation and is shared only among the parties involved in the mediation process. The Mediator will facilitate communication between the farmer and their creditor(s), guide them through the mediation process, and remain neutral throughout. The Mediator will work collaboratively with the Financial Consultant to understand the context of the file, including the recovery plan developed by the farmer and the Financial Consultant. The Mediator will lead the mediation meeting and work with the parties toward a mutually acceptable solution. When the farmer and their creditor(s) reach an agreement, the Mediator will prepare the written arrangement and obtain the signatures of all participants

title: Montenegro – Radiotherapy devices and supplies – Supply of HDR Brachytherapy System within LIFEGATE project
description: Cardiovascular and oncological diseases remain the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region. According to GLOBOCAN 2020 data, Montenegro recorded 3,184 new cancer cases and 1,765 cancer-related deaths. With the expected increase in cancer incidence, an ageing population, and existing healthcare challenges, improving early detection, diagnostics, and access to specialised treatment is becoming increasingly important. The Clinical Centre of Montenegro (CCM), as the country's leading tertiary healthcare institution, plays a crucial role in providing specialised oncology services. Through this project, CCM aims to strengthen its diagnostic and treatment capacities, introduce advanced medical technologies, and improve the quality and accessibility of cancer care. A particular focus is placed on early lung cancer detection and the improvement of radiotherapy treatment, including the application of advanced techniques such as stereotactic radiotherapy and brachytherapy. These approaches are expected to contribute to more precise and effective treatment, improved patient outcomes, and better survival rates. Brachytherapy represents an important component of the planned improvements at CCM, offering opportunities to enhance treatment efficiency and quality for patients with various malignancies, particularly cervical, prostate, oesophageal, and lung cancers. The project will also support the development of innovative digital solutions, improved cancer prevention and screening programmes, and the modernisation of healthcare infrastructure through new equipment and professional training. Through cooperation with healthcare institutions in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Clinical Centre of Montenegro will contribute to strengthening cross-border collaboration, exchanging medical expertise, and promoting common standards in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Ultimately, the project aims to improve access to modern oncology services, enhance treatment outcomes, and strengthen the long-term capacities of the Clinical Centre of Montenegro, benefiting patients in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region.

title: STEC Media
description: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service is part of a science-based national system to ensure food safety and food defense. FSIS ensures food safety through the authorities of the Federal Meat Inspection Act, the Poultry Products Inspection Act, and the Egg Products Inspection Act, as well as humane animal handling through the Humane Methods of Slaughter Act. As such this RFI seeks to gather information on commercially available STEC colony isolation procedures that increase the likelihood of identifying and isolating a variety of STEC in raw beef or other food products, regardless of serogroup, from a mixed population. FSIS seeks to understand the level of granularity in STEC confirmation protocols, including selective media that do not rely on STEC serogroup. Please review the attached documents for more information.
